Agent spawn is a face verb — fixing #1872 (Dock detection + transcript loss)

Bugs·seedling·proposed·JUL 17, 2026

Both #1872 mechanisms share one cause: spawning an agent through a path with no agent semantics. The fix is layered per srid's steer — the faces (kolu mcp / kolu-tui) own agent-spawn as a first-class verb; kaval-tui composes env instead of forwarding it; kaval stays a dumb PTY daemon and gains only bookkeeping it should have had anyway.

Contents

  • Why the kolu face never had this bug
  • The fix, layered (each change names what it makes inexpressible)
  • Doctrine until the fix ships

Issue #1872, two proven mechanisms when an agent is spawned as the PTY’s root command (kaval-tui create -- claude …):

  • A · Dock detection dead. The daemon receives the exact argv at spawn (ptyHostSurface requires it) and drops it — entry.lastCommand starts undefined (ptyHost.ts:663) and its only writer is the OSC 633;E parse (:710-727), a mark only kolu’s rc-hooked shell emits (shell.ts:218). A shell-less PTY never learns its own command. Second lock: padi’s sensors compute shellIdle = foregroundPid === pid assuming pid is a shell (sensors.ts:394-402) — a command-rooted PTY reads as “idle at prompt” and detection is suppressed even if the command were known.
  • B · Transcript loss (data loss). kaval-tui’s create composer copies the caller’s whole process.env verbatim (create.ts:55-57). From an orchestrating Claude session, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 rides in; the spawned claude self-classifies as a nested child and never persists its conversation (A/B-proven on #1872). Shell-mode create leaks identically.

Why the kolu face never had this bug

PadiCreateInputSchema is { cwd?, parentId? } — no command, no env (surface.ts:513-518). An agent launched through kolu/mcp is necessarily create-shell-then-send: the rc hooks run (633;E fires), and env comes from padi’s own cleanEnv() (ptyHost/index.ts:397), never the caller’s. Both illegal states are unspellable at the face wire schema. That absence is load-bearing — the kolu-mcp docstring saying “(command, cwd, parent)” overstates and must be corrected to match.

The fix, layered (each change names what it makes inexpressible)

Layer Change Kills
Faces (kolu mcp now; kolu-tui when it ships) Agent launch is a first-class verb — internally create(shell) + send + detection seed. Never a command param on create. The mcp face already has this shape; kolu-tui inherits it as a requirement of the kolu-cli plan. “Agent as PTY root” and “agent under caller env” have no spelling at any face.
kaval-tui composer (client, not daemon) Compose env, don’t forward it — the way its own remote composer already does (minimal canonical base + explicit additions). Caller additions become an explicit --env K=V. At minimum: never verbatim-forward when a -- command is given. The caller’s ambient session identity cannot reach the child — including agents that don’t exist yet. (A CLAUDE_* deny-list is rejected: blacklist = the class survives every new orchestrator.)
kaval (daemon — dumb bookkeeping only) Seed entry.lastCommand (+ initial title) from spawn argv and publish on the command channel; the 633;E mark stays the live writer (last-writer-wins, seed writes first). “A PTY whose own daemon forgot what it spawned.” lastCommand === undefined regains a single meaning: nothing has run yet in a shell.
padi sensors (only if command-rooted PTYs ever become sensor-visible) shellIdle becomes conditional on a typed shell-rooted fact of the PTY; for command-rooted PTYs, foregroundPid === pid means “the agent IS foreground” — the opposite reading. The ambient assumption “root is a shell” becomes a checked fact, never a silent misreading.
upstream (Claude Code) File the A/B evidence: classifying “I am a child session, don’t persist” from an inherited ambient env var is fragile by design — any env-forwarding intermediary (ssh, sudo -E, a Makefile) silently destroys a transcript. kolu’s composition mitigates, not cures. — (out of our tree; recorded so the residual is explicit)

kaval remains a dumb PTY daemon throughout: it gains no agent semantics, no env opinion (it spawns what the composer sends, verbatim) — only the bookkeeping of not discarding a fact it was handed.

Doctrine until the fix ships

  • kaval-tui create -- <agent> is forbidden from any agent session (it hits both mechanisms); the /kolu skill’s neutral mention becomes a warning.
  • Shell-mode create + send is not sufficient either — the shell inherits the orchestrator’s vars; the launch line must scrub (unset CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION CLAUDECODE CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID first), or use a daemon-spawned (restored) shell.
  • Each workaround edit carries a ships-with marker so the text is deleted when the structural fix merges.

Sequencing

(1) kaval-tui composed env — closes the data loss for every kaval-tui path; (2) mcp docstring fix + the kolu-cli plan pins agent-spawn-as-verb for the tui face; (3) skill doctrine; (4) kaval argv seeding (+ the sensor discrimination only when needed). Grounded by a 16-agent a-f-p + perfection lens run (13 findings, 0 refuted).
